filing_playbook.action: Confirm in writing with San Francisco Planning whether a new CUA application is required or whether the September 2022 denial can be reconsidered with revised plans or operating conditions.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Explain that you are the new applicant for 779 Bush St and reference the September 2022 ABC referral denial (file 2022-008099MIS). Ask whether Planning will accept a new CUA application under Section 202.12 for the laundromat conversion, or whether the prior denial can be appealed or reconsidered if the concept or commitments change. Request the name of the planner who will handle the case and the current CUA application fee.

filing_playbook.action: Form the legal entity (LLC or corporation) with the California Secretary of State and obtain an EIN from the IRS.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File Articles of Organization (LLC, $70) or Articles of Incorporation (corporation, $100) online through the California Secretary of State bizfile portal. Within 90 days file the Statement of Information ($20 LLC, $25 corporation). Apply for an Employer Identification Number (EIN) online at IRS.gov the same day; it is free and issued immediately. Use the entity name and EIN for all subsequent filings.

filing_playbook.action: Register the business with the San Francisco Treasurer and obtain a Business Account Number (BAN), and file a Fictitious Business Name statement if the bar name differs from the entity name.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register online with the SF Treasurer within 30 days of forming the entity. The fee is tiered by projected gross receipts ($55–$700); estimate conservatively. The BAN is required for every other city permit. If the public-facing bar name differs from the legal entity name, file a Fictitious Business Name statement with the County Clerk in person or by mail, then publish it once a week for four weeks in a court-approved newspaper and file proof of publication within 45 days. Banks and ABC require the filed FBN statement.

filing_playbook.action: File the building permit application for tenant improvements and change of use with the Department of Building Inspection.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the building permit application with plans stamped by a licensed architect. The permit fee is a percentage of construction valuation (estimate $800–$15,000). Separate plumbing, electrical and mechanical permits are pulled by licensed contractors. Budget 1–4 months for plan review and approval.

timeline_cost.notes: These figures are the time and government cost to obtain the Conditional Use Authorization, health permit and building permit for tenant improvements—the three approvals in the entitlement path—when they are granted. The CUA is the critical path: 120–300 days from filing to final approval (including pre-application, environmental review, noticing, hearing and the 30-day appeal period), with a city fee of approximately $3,100–$15,000 depending on construction cost. The health permit adds 14–45 days and $470 after the CUA is approved. The building permit for tenant improvements adds 14–120 days and $800–$15,000 (percentage of construction cost) and is processed in parallel with or after the CUA. These figures do not include the ABC licence, which cannot be filed until the CUA is granted; add 60–240 days and $1,000–$1,600 for a new Type 41/42 (beer/wine), or 90–240 days and $17,000–$450,000 to purchase and transfer a Type 47/48 (full bar). The alcohol licence type and transaction method are not stated, so no ABC time or cost is included here. Also not included: entity formation, business registration, FBN, seller's permit, RBS training, workers' comp, music licences, sign permit, and any costs to remediate the laundromat or purchase a transferred liquor licence. Professional fees (architect, expediter, ABC broker, lawyer) are not government costs and are not included.

records_summary: The records show a significant obstacle at this address: an ABC Type 48 (bar) referral was denied by Planning in September 2022—two months ago—because Planning Code Section 202.12 requires a Conditional Use Authorization to change the use of a laundromat, even though bar use is principally permitted on the ground floor in the RC-4 zoning district. The block is densely developed with alcohol uses: 24 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft (92 within 1,000 ft) and 5 bars within 500 ft. Nearby bar approvals in RC-4 (801 Bush, 845 Bush, 895 Bush) were for continuations of existing bar uses or transfers, not new conversions requiring discretionary review.
data_gaps: No hearing records or decision text available for the September 2022 denial to understand Planning's full reasoning
No conditions data extracted from nearby bar approvals to understand typical operating restrictions
Census tract undue-concentration status for ABC purposes not confirmed by the records
No discretionary review history available for other laundromat conversions in RC-4 to gauge hearing outcomes
